chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibnarrated from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When it is the Day of Resurrection, a neck (group) of the people will stand and come to the Door of Paradise and knock it. So it will be said to them, 'Who are you?' They will say, 'We are the people of patience.' It will be said to them, 'Upon what were you patient?' They will say, 'We were patient in obeying Allah and we were patient in refraining from disobeying Allah.'
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'They are speaking the truth. Admit them into Paradise.'
Only those will be given their reward in full without reckoning, who are patient.
ai.seo_question: How are the patient rewarded on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the dual nature of true patience (sabr) as both active perseverance in worship and passive restraint from sin, a concept central to Shia ethical theology. The hadith highlights the eschatological reward for this balanced piety, linking it directly to the Quranic promise of boundless recompense, thereby emphasizing that spiritual endurance is the key to entering Paradise.
